hook: A U.S. Air Force Special Operations gunship crew filed this MISREP after observing an IR-signature-emitting object fly through their sensor field of view at high speed during an AGM-176 Griffin missile shot over Ayn Al Asad Airbase, Iraq, on 20 September 2024.
why_it_matters: This report is notable because the UAP encounter occurred during an active weapons employment event — between munition release and impact — placing the object in a contested, kinetic airspace at a precise and documented moment. The crew's observation that the UAP's path 'appeared predetermined and not in response to' the aircraft's detection raises a behavioral question that the document explicitly leaves unresolved. Additionally, the report notes uncertainty about whether a secondary object detached from the primary UAP before it left the sensor field of view, a detail that the official description does not highlight.

key_findings.finding: The UAP flew through the aircraft's sensor field of view between the release of the AGM-176 Griffin missile and its impact on the target, placing it in the engagement corridor at a specific operational moment.

quotes.text: UAP FLEW THROUGH (b)(1)1.4a SENSOR IN BETWEEN MUNITION RELEASE AND MUNITION IMPACT

RECEIVED A CALL FOR FIRE AT APPROXIMATELY 2025Z TO EMPLOY AN AGM-176. AFTER WEAPONS RELEASE, THE WEAPONS SYSTEMS OFFICER (WSO) AND COMBAT SYSTEMS OFFICER (CSO) OBSERVED AN UNIDENTIFIED OBJECT "FLY" THROUGH THE AIRCRAFT SENSORS AT A HIGH RATE OF SPEED.

key_findings.finding: The UAP produced an infrared lens flare on both the MX-20 and MX-25 targeting sensors, which the crew interpreted as evidence of a significant heat source.

quotes.text: UAP CREATED IR LENS FLARE ON MX-20 & MX-25 SENSORS, INDICATING A SIGNIFICANT HEAT SOURCE. THE UAP MOVED AT A HIGH RATE OF SPEED THROUGH THE SENSOR FIELD OF VIEW.
UAP Signatures: IR SIGNATURE DETECTABLE BY MX-20 & MX-25

key_findings.finding: The UAP's trajectory was assessed as predetermined and non-reactive — it did not appear to respond to the aircraft's detection or presence.

quotes.text: UAP Reaction to Observation, Interrogation, Engagement (yes/no; if yes, describe): NONE OBSERVED; PATH OF MOVEMENT APPEARED PREDETERMINED AND NOT IN RESPONSE TO (b)(1)1.4a's DETECTION
UAP Response to Observer Actions: NONE OBSERVED

key_findings.finding: It remained unknown at the time of the report whether a secondary object detached from the primary UAP immediately before it exited the sensor field of view.

quotes.text: IT IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME WHETHER AN OBJECT DETACHED ITSELF FROM THE PRIMARY UAP IMMEDIATELY BEFORE LEAVING THE SENSOR FIELD OF VIEW.
UAP Anomalous Characteristics/ Behaviors: IT IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME WHETHER AN OBJECT DETACHED ITSELF FROM THE PRIMARY UAP IMMEDIATELY BEFORE LEAVING THE SENSOR FIELD OF VIEW.

key_findings.finding: No radar interrogation of the UAP was performed, no other parties reported an additional aircraft in the airspace, and the crew did not reobserve the UAP after the initial event.

quotes.text: Observation Interrogation of UAP (yes/no; if yes list sensor(s) and returns):: NO
Third-party Observers and/or Reporters: NO PARTIES REPORTED AN ADDITIONAL AIRCRAFT IN THE AIRSPACE WITH (b)(1)1.4a
THE CREW MAINTAINED LASER ENERGY UNTIL THE MUNITION IMPACTED ITS DESIRED TARGET. (b)(1)1.4a DID NOT REOBSERVE THE UAP.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The MISREP was explicitly submitted to and approved for release by AARO, and the UAP event serial number references CENTCOM coordination with AARO's reporting pipeline.
The document carries SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY classification throughout, indicating the UAP report was shared within the Five Eyes intelligence community.
